newsitem.title: USA: Bill introduced to create Amtrak trust fund.
newsitem.headline: Bill introduced to create Amtrak trust fund.

text.p: A bill to create a capital improvement trust fund for Amtrak, the national rail passenger service, was introduced Thursday by Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth.
"A secure source of capital funding is critical if we are to strengthen Amtrak and reduce its reliance on federal operating support," Roth, a Delaware Republican, said in a statement.

Money for the trust fund would come from transferring one-half cent of the 4.3 cents-per-gallon federal gasoline tax now going to the government's general funds, Roth said. The fund would be used for upgrading Amtrak's routes to permit high speed rail service and to buy new rail cars and locomotives.
Amtrak Chairman Thomas Downs told a House hearing Wednesday that Amtrak was dangerously short of funds and its survival was threatened unless Congress acted.

Amtrak, which has never made a profit, gets much of its operating funds in federal subsidies approved by Congress, but the amount has been cut in recent years and is supposed to be eliminated by 2002.
Amtrak was created by Congress three decades ago to take over intercity rail passenger service from private railroads.
